variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The cube slides back and forth along a line that passes through the target; every time it crosses the target line counts as one arrival at the target. The goal instruction names the ordinal N (second, third, fifth...). The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the cube is on its way back toward the target, so the press lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time. An episode starts in A: at the first step (empty memory, gripper raised out of the frame and not yet above the button) choose A 'move to the top of the button to prepare'. No point is needed. At every later step (gripper is already positioned above the button, fingers closed), first update memory as instructed (crossings, cube_side, peak_speed, last_cube_x, last_t), then decide using the updated crossings and peak_speed values and the cube motion: - Determine the cube's motion from a pair of positions, in this order. Form the pair first: when two or more frames are shown at this step, the pair is the last two frames shown; when exactly one frame is shown, the earlier member of the pair is the carried-in memory (position last_cube_x, side cube_side, time last_t) and the later member is the shown frame, so the x change is cube_x minus last_cube_x and the timestep gap is t of this frame minus last_t. cube_x is always the SECOND number of the cube's [y, x] position, and target_x the SECOND number of the target's [y, x] position; the first numbers are y and are never compared. (1) If the cube is on different sides of the target in the two members of the pair (for a single-frame step: the carried-in cube_side differs from the side in this frame), it is passing the target right now and its next motion is outward: classify it as NOT IN THE PRESS WINDOW, whatever the distances are. (2) Otherwise compute |cube_x - target_x| at each member of the pair, take the change (later minus earlier) and divide by the timestep gap between them: this is the outward rate in px per timestep (negative if the distance shrank). Always divide by the timestep spacing; never judge by the raw pixel change between frames. Then compute distance = |cube_x - target_x| at the scene at this step, and lead = distance / peak_speed, the number of timesteps the cube would need at its peak speed to reach the target (if peak_speed is 0, treat lead as very large). The press is issued a fixed lead before arrival, about 20 to 27 timesteps, whether the cube is finishing its outward sweep or already returning, so classify: if the outward rate is zero or negative (returning or stopped) AND lead <= 27, the cube is IN THE PRESS WINDOW. If the outward rate is positive but at most about 60% of peak_speed (clearly slowed, finishing its outward sweep) AND lead <= 24, the cube is IN THE PRESS WINDOW. Otherwise the cube is NOT IN THE PRESS WINDOW: returning but lead > 27 (it turned around far out and is still too many timesteps away; it will be pressed at a later decision step), moving outward at more than about 60% of peak_speed (still sweeping out near full speed), or moving outward with lead > 24 (too far out for its speed). - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if crossings == N-1 AND the cube is classified IN THE PRESS WINDOW above. No point is needed. A step that shows a single frame is common right after the step at which the cube was seen nearing its extreme; when crossings == N-1 and the pair formed from memory places the cube IN THE PRESS WINDOW, that single-frame step is the press moment, not a reason to wait. Showing only one frame is never by itself a reason to choose B. - Otherwise choose B 'remain static'. This covers: crossings < N-1 (even if the cube is heading toward the target, let it pass), and crossings == N-1 while the cube is NOT IN THE PRESS WINDOW (including the case where the (N-1)th crossing lies between the last two frames, so the cube is just passing the target and about to sweep outward; and the case where the cube has already turned around but is still more than 27 peak-speed timesteps from the target, which is pressed at a later step). If crossings somehow exceeds N-1, or the situation matches no rule above, choose C immediately if the cube is heading toward the target, otherwise B. Never choose A after the first step.

fields.name: crossings
fields.description: Take the crossings count carried in (0 at the first step, since memory is empty). Build the sequence: the carried-in cube_side (skip if memory is empty), then the side (cube_x < target_x -> smaller_x, cube_x > target_x -> larger_x, where cube_x and target_x are the SECOND numbers of the cube's and the target's [y, x] positions) of each frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. Add 1 for every consecutive pair in that sequence whose side differs. Write the result. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: Number of times, since t=0 and up to and including the scene at this decision step, that the cube's x-coordinate has moved from one side of the target's x-coordinate to the other (cube_x and target_x are the SECOND numbers of the cube's and the target's [y, x] positions; a crossing happens between two consecutive observed frames when the sign of cube_x minus target_x flips; being near the target without flipping is not a crossing). Each crossing is one arrival of the cube at the target. At step #1 the value is 0. It increases only at the step whose observed frames contain the flip. e.g. 2

fields.name: cube_side
fields.description: The side of the target line the cube is on in the last frame shown at this step (the scene at this decision step): 'smaller_x' if cube_x < target_x, 'larger_x' if cube_x > target_x. cube_x is the SECOND number of the cube's [y, x] position and target_x the SECOND number of the target's [y, x] position; the first numbers are y and are never used here. Worked example: cube at [131, 61] and target at [107, 145] -> compare 61 with 145 -> 61 < 145 -> smaller_x. Overwrite it every step; at the first step read it from the single frame shown. e.g. smaller_x
fields.annotation: Which side of the target line the cube is on in the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown): 'smaller_x' if cube_x < target_x, 'larger_x' if cube_x > target_x. cube_x and target_x are the SECOND numbers of the cube's and the target's [y, x] positions (the first numbers are y and are never used here): a cube at [131, 61] and a target at [107, 145] give 61 and 145, and 61 < 145 -> 'smaller_x'. At step #1 it is read from the t=0 frame. e.g. smaller_x

fields.name: peak_speed
fields.description: Take the carried-in peak_speed (0 if memory is empty). Build the frame list: first the carried-in position (last_cube_x at time last_t) if memory is not empty, then every frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. cube_x is always the SECOND number of the cube's [y, x] position. For every consecutive pair in that list write the x change |cube_x(later) - cube_x(earlier)| and the timestep gap; if the gap is at least 8, write the quotient rounded to one decimal with halves rounding up (3.875 -> 3.9); if the gap is below 8 timesteps (common just before the decision scene, where detection wobble dominates), skip that pair. Write the largest of the carried-in value and all the counted quotients. It never decreases. At the first step (empty memory, one frame) write 0. e.g. 2.0
fields.annotation: The fastest cube x-speed observed so far in the episode, in pixels of x per timestep. Take ALL observed frames of the episode in time order, from the t=0 scene up to and including the scene at this decision step, including the pair formed by the scene at one decision step and the first frame shown at the next (this cross-step pair is what last_cube_x and last_t are kept for). Only pairs of consecutive frames whose timestep gap is at least 8 count; pairs closer than 8 timesteps (such as the 1-, 3- or 5-timestep gap just before a decision scene) are skipped because detection wobble dominates them. For each counted pair compute |cube_x(later) - cube_x(earlier)| divided by the gap, rounded to one decimal with halves rounding up (3.875 -> 3.9); write the largest such quotient seen so far. cube_x is the SECOND number of the cube's [y, x] position. At step #1 there is only one frame, so write 0. The value never decreases; it changes only at a step whose counted pairs contain a faster quotient than any before. e.g. 2.0

fields.name: last_cube_x
fields.description: Write the cube's x-coordinate in the last frame shown at this step (the scene at this decision step), as a plain number. x is the SECOND number of the cube's [y, x] position: a cube at [85, 52] gives 52. Overwrite it every step; at the first step read it from the single frame shown. It is read at the next step as the earlier member of the pair with the first frame shown there, both for peak_speed and, when that step shows a single frame, for judging the cube's motion. e.g. 52
fields.annotation: The cube's x-coordinate (the SECOND number of its [y, x] position; a cube at [85, 52] gives 52) in the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown), as a plain number. Overwritten at every step; at step #1 it is read from the t=0 frame. e.g. 206

fields.name: last_t
fields.description: Write the timestep index t of the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown). Overwrite it every step; at the first step write 0. It is read at the next step to compute the timestep gap between the carried-in last_cube_x and the first frame shown there: that gap decides whether the pair counts for peak_speed (gap at least 8) and gives the rate for the motion judgement at a single-frame step. e.g. 503
fields.annotation: The timestep index t of the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown). Overwritten at every step; at step #1 it is 0. e.g. 54

history.critique:
the policy prompt for subgoal
  Two steps where the (N-1)th crossing happened inside the step's own frames went wrong, in opposite directions, and both come from the motion test. In the first, the goal asked for the fourth arrival; the carried crossings was 2, the frames showed the cube turn around at the near end, sweep back across the target (crossings now 3 = N-1) and run out to the far end, where the last two frames, only four timesteps apart, showed it drifting outward by two pixels. The recorded subgoal was C, but the instruction treated any increase in |cube_x - target_x| as 'moving away' and sent the policy to B. The memory was correctly written as crossings=3. In the second, the goal also asked for the fourth arrival; the carried crossings was 2, and the frames showed the cube come back from the near end and cross the target between the last two frames (the second-to-last frame on one side at about 20 px from the target, the last frame just past it by about 2 px). The recorded subgoal was B, but because |cube_x - target_x| shrank from the second-to-last frame to the last, the instruction read it as 'moving toward' and chose C. Both are SUFFICIENCY failures of the subgoal instruction: memory and the step held what was needed, but the motion test misread it. Replace the motion test with this. First check whether the cube's side of the target differs between the last two frames shown; if it does, the cube is passing the target right now and will move away next, so it counts as moving away regardless of the distances. Otherwise compute |cube_x - target_x| at the last two frames: decreasing means moving toward; increasing means moving away, EXCEPT that an outward drift of fewer than about 5 px between the last two frames (under about 1 px per timestep, which only happens at the far end of the swing where the cube is slowing to turn around) counts as stationary at the turnaround. Also keep treating an equal distance as the turnaround. Then the choice stands as before: choose C when the updated crossings == N-1 and the cube is moving toward the target or is at the turnaround (including the small-drift case); choose B when crossings < N-1, or when crossings == N-1 and the cube is moving away by more than that small drift (which includes every case where the crossing lies between the last two frames, and the outward sweep right after a crossing, where consecutive frames move 7 px or more). The rule 'crossings == N-1 AND not moving away -> C' is kept; the rule that any increase in distance means moving away is dropped, and the rule that a decreasing distance means moving toward is dropped for the case where the side flips between the last two frames.

refused
  One step proposed that C should be chosen only when crossings == N-1 was already the carried-in value, and that a step whose own frames contain the (N-1)th crossing must always answer B. That is refused: in another episode of this minibatch the recorded press was chosen at a step whose own frames contained the (N-1)th crossing, with the cube out at the far end of its swing and nearly stopped. What distinguishes the two is not when the crossing was counted but the cube's motion at the last frames (just passing the target and about to sweep away, versus slowed to the turnaround), so the fix is the motion test above rather than a carried-in-only condition. The same step also reported nothing missing from memory and its crossings value was correct, so no memory change is passed on.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  The failures all happened at the same kind of moment: the required number of arrivals minus one had already been counted, the gripper was closed above the button, and the last two frames showed the cube still creeping outward slowly near the end of its swing. In two of these the recorded choice was to press, in one it was to wait, and the current classification rule (absolute pixel change under about 5 px between frames, or under about 1 px per timestep) could not separate them, because in all three the outward drift was between 0.7 and 1.0 px per timestep while the frame spacing varied from 5 to 12 timesteps. This breaks SUFFICIENCY. What actually separates them is the cube itself: a slow cube (fastest observed speed below about 2.5 px per timestep) takes much longer to turn around and come back, so a slow outward drift still leaves too much time and the press must wait until the cube is seen returning; a fast cube (fastest observed speed about 2.5 px per timestep or more) is at the turnaround when its outward drift has fallen to about 1 px per timestep or less, and the press must go now. Replace the MOVING AWAY / AT THE TURNAROUND test with this: compute the change in |cube_x - target_x| between the last two frames and divide by the number of timesteps between them, giving an outward rate (negative if the distance shrank). Then, with crossings == N-1 and the cube on the same side of the target in both frames: choose C if the distance is decreasing or unchanged (the cube is returning or stopped at the turnaround), regardless of peak_speed; choose C if the outward rate is positive but at most about 1 px per timestep AND the memory's peak_speed is at least about 2.5 px per timestep (fast cube at its turnaround); choose B if the outward rate is positive and peak_speed is below about 2.5 (slow cube, wait until the distance is seen decreasing); choose B if the outward rate is clearly above 1 px per timestep (still sweeping out), whatever the cube's speed. Keep the rule that different sides in the last two frames means the cube is just passing the target and B is chosen, and keep all the crossings < N-1 behaviour unchanged. Drop the clause that measures the threshold as an absolute number of pixels between frames; always divide by the timestep spacing. Memory must be updated first (crossings, cube_side, peak_speed) and the updated values used.

refused
  Three steps reported the slow-outward-drift ambiguity and each proposed a fix that fits only its own step. One proposed that any increase in the cube-target distance, however small, means still moving away and B; that contradicts the two steps where the cube was drifting outward at under 1 px per timestep and the recorded answer was to press. Another proposed classifying purely by outward rate per timestep with a threshold around 1 px per timestep; that contradicts the slow-cube step where the rate was 0.8 and the recorded answer was to wait. The third proposed treating a clear drop in speed from the previous frame pair as decelerating toward the turnaround and pressing; the slow-cube step also showed a drop in speed and still required waiting. None of these per-step criteria is carried forward as stated; they are replaced by the single rule above that combines outward rate with the cube's peak speed kept in memory, which agrees with every recorded step in the minibatch. The memory values the policy wrote at the failed steps matched the annotation, so no change to crossings or cube_side is passed on.
